status: candidate frozen references; derived and cross-checked by the author TASK before the fixture's RS-OPE-REF was solved against them, not yet independently refuted
specification: DEL-09-01 (the member states of RS-OPE and RS-OPE-REF; EQ-1 and EQ-2 for RS-OPE-REF; EQ-3 on RS-OPE-REF - RS-SUS)
inputs: the specification's statements (§3.2, §4.1, §5.1, §8, §8.1), transcribed in the generator; no fixture model file and no product output is read

checks.member states: for each member of RS-OPE and RS-OPE-REF, the consumed material point(s), E, nu, G, the thermal strain and (RS-OPE-REF) the analysis-basis reason equal `member_states`
checks.EQ-1: in RS-OPE-REF, the sum of the global Z support action components over every support, RS-VS1 and RS-CE1 included, equals W_total
checks.EQ-2: in RS-OPE-REF, the horizontal (X, Y) resultant is zero and the support action moment resultant about the origin equals reaction_moment_about_origin
checks.EQ-3: on every published signed component row, RS-EXP = RS-OPE-REF - RS-SUS; magnitude rows equal the norm of the combined components; rows the combination withholds are excluded and listed; the identity establishes the combination's algebra and nothing about either solve

criterion: EQ-1, EQ-2, EQ-3: the r1_ce package's (DEC-024/DEC-026), |observed - expected| <= 1e-9 * |expected|, a zero row against 1e-9 * zero_scale; member states: the consumer states its a priori rounding bound

crosscheck.check: RS-OPE-REF's modulus is the 20 degC point's 200 GPa on every member
the thermal strain from 20 to 210 degC is 57/25000 = alpha * 190 (the ratio form's denominator is 1)
RS-OPE and RS-OPE-REF have the same thermal strain on every member
RS-P180 has zero eigenstrain in both cases
the two cases' moduli differ on every member: ratio 1883/2000
25 members of each case have an operating temperature; RS-P180 has none
validation/references/reference_system_r1_ce/references.json states EQ-1 and EQ-2 for exactly RS-SUS, RS-OPE and RS-SAM
validation/references/reference_system_r1_ce/references.json: W_total is the sum of its member and component weight records
validation/references/reference_system_r1_ce/references.json: the weight moment about the origin is (-S_y, S_x, 0)
validation/references/reference_system_r1_ce/references.json: the reaction moment about the origin is minus the weight moment

distinguishing.rule: the two cases carry the same thermal strain and differ in modulus only; a reader of the published load reference state tells them apart by the consumed point(s), E and G, and by RS-OPE-REF's stated analysis-basis reason

grounds: RS-OPE-REF's W is the self-weight of the same members with the same gravity and the same component weights as RS-SUS, RS-OPE and RS-SAM (spec §8.1)
a free-length thermal state is an eigenstrain: it applies no external load, so the reaction resultant is unchanged by temperature, whatever the modulus
every pressure closure transfers to the wall, so each region is self-equilibrated under pressure (spec §9.2, EQ-2)
RS-CE1's 9000 N is the same support action in every case and adds no weight

eq3.label: RS-EXP expansion: RS-OPE-REF - RS-SUS, the difference of two solved states on the 20 degC modulus
eq3.identity: on every published signed component row (support force and moment components, translation and rotation components, element end-force components), RS-EXP = RS-OPE-REF - RS-SUS; magnitude rows are recomputed from the combined components; rows the combination withholds, such as tie-rod forces, are excluded
eq3.both_operands_on_one_material_basis: every member of RS-SUS and RS-OPE-REF selects the 20 degC point
eq3.what_it_establishes: the combination's algebra: RS-EXP is the row-by-row difference of the two published solved states; it establishes nothing about either solve, and RS-EXP is the difference of two independently solved equilibria, not a solution of the system under the load difference
